transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-12
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Liam O'Reilly (Redwood CSM); Dr. Ellen Park (Horizon CTO), Rahul Mehta (Infra), Sofia Gutierrez (Procurement), Ben Carter (ML)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in to align on annual commitment, add regions (EU + APAC), and sizing the Dedicated capacity uplift. Discussed timelines for procurement and next benchmarks.

Topics:
- Current committed capacity utilization and burst patterns
- APAC latency and options to add ap-southeast-1 region
- Pricing for additional reserved GPUs and burst pools
- Contract extension terms (term length vs discount)
- Security / compliance notes for expansion

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Ellen: Hi, Ellen here.
[00:07] Rahul: Rahul, infra team.
[00:10] Sofia: Sofia from procurement.
[00:12] Ben: Ben, ML.
[00:15] Jordan: Jordan Kim, SE at Redwood.
[00:18] Liam: Liam O'Reilly, CSM.
[00:20] Maya: Perfect. The goal today is to confirm the renewal numbers and plan the region additions you flagged — eu-west-2 and ap-southeast-1 — and make sure the pricing we proposed fits your procurement cadence.
[00:32] Ellen: Yep, that's right. Our main concern is latency for APAC users and also keeping unit cost manageable. We saw a couple of tail latency spikes during the last holiday window.
[00:41] Jordan: Right, and those spikes align with the larger prompt sizes and high concurrency around 200 rps peaks. On Dedicated, we can either add a small APAC pool or route to hosted in APAC region, there are tradeoffs.
[00:54] Rahul: Can you run through the tradeoffs again? We prefer dedicated for sensitive workflows.
[00:58] Jordan: Sure. Dedicated APAC pool gives you predictable latency and data isolation — everything stays in your VPC if you choose Private or Dedicated inside your cloud account. The downside is you pay reserved capacity even in quiet periods unless you configure burst policies. If you go hosted APAC, it's cheaper short term but you lose strict isolation and there's potential for throttling at peak.
[01:18] Ben: Also curious on model variants — we use a quantized variant for cost but are we seeing quality delta when we switch?
[01:25] Jordan: There's typically a small perf/quality tradeoff. For most classification and extraction tasks you won't notice. For the long-form summarizer with 8k context you might. We can run the 8k benchmark on your Dedicated pool.
[01:36] Ellen: That would be great.
[01:38] Maya: Action: Jordan to run 8k context benchmark on a 2xV100 equivalent pool.
[01:42] Rahul: Quick note on networking — our on-prem systems peer to cloud via a fixed egress IP list. If we spin up APAC Dedicated, will we need additional peering or CIDR changes?
[01:51] Jordan: Good question. You'll likely need VPC peering or private link — Rahul, we'd want your network CIDRs and security team on the thread. There may be a small NAT change.
[02:04] Rahul: Sounds good. I'll loop in the network folks.
[02:06] Maya: On pricing, the renewal proposal had a 12-month extension with 15% discount for a 3x reserved commit. If you want to step up capacity mid-contract we can include a true-up clause or pre-agreed uplift discounts.
[02:20] Sofia: Procurement likes predictable buckets. We prefer a fixed committed amount and a small burst pool for spikes. How does the burst billing work?
[02:27] Maya: Burst is meter-based, charged at lower per-token than pure on-demand but higher than reserved. You can set a budget threshold to auto-turn off burst or alert.
[02:36] Ben: Any penalties for term changes if we reduce capacity after renewal?
[02:39] Maya: The committed portion is paid; reducing isn't retroactive. We can add a mid-term renegotiation clause but it affects the discount rate.
[02:47] Ellen: For security, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and KMS key control for log retention. We were happy with the SOC 2 cert last year, any changes with region expansion?
[02:58] Liam: No change to SOC 2 coverage, but for key management if you want customer-managed keys in new regions we’ll need to enable CMK in those regions and coordinate with your KMS team.
[03:09] Rahul: Do you offer HSM-backed keys on Dedicated?
[03:12] Jordan: Yes, HSM/KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we support envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys unless you bring your own.
[03:22] Sofia: Are there any additional compliance costs for EU or APAC data residency?
[03:26] Maya: Not extra platform fees, but data transfer costs and the cost of running dedicated infra in those regions will reflect local pricing. We included regional multipliers in the quote.
[03:36] Ellen: Procurement timeline — we need terms signed by end of April if possible. Can Redwood compress approvals?
[03:42] Maya: We can commit to a 48-hour turnaround on final quote and start a contract redline in parallel.
[03:47] Sofia: That helps. Also need a named approver list for our legal team. I'll send that by Thursday.
[03:53] Maya: Great. Jordan, any open technical risks we should call out?
[03:57] Jordan: For expansion, the main items: (1) VPC peering and CIDR constraints; (2) potential cold-start latency if you scale pools too quickly; (3) model compatibility for quantized kernels — a few older ops on your custom model may not be optimized. We recommend a small canary in the new region before full traffic cutover.
[04:15] Ben: How long to spin up a Dedicated pool in a new region?
[04:18] Jordan: Typically 2-3 business days for provision + warm-up; if you want pre-warmed reserved nodes it can be done during onboarding to avoid warmup.
[04:27] Rahul: We do want pre-warmed, holiday windows killed us last time.
[04:30] Maya: We'll add a pre-warm option to the quote.
[04:33] Ellen: On the contract, are we locked to a single model family? We might want to swap to a newer open model mid-term.
[04:40] Maya: You can pin model versions per route; swap is supported. If you move to a materially different model family that changes compute assumptions, we might need to re-evaluate pricing but that's standard.
[04:52] Ben: Regarding telemetry, can you expose per-route token-level cost and tail-latency? We want that in Grafana.
[04:58] Jordan: Yes, we provide token-level breakdowns in the Console and can send a Grafana export via our metrics endpoint or a prometheus scrape. Some metric names are a bit noisy in the export — it's usually fine once we map them.
[05:12] Ellen: Any blockers on our side?
[05:15] Rahul: Network confirmation and procurement signatory list.
[05:17] Sofia: Also final SOW language about SLA credits on Dedicated; need to confirm uptime SLA thresholds.
[05:23] Liam: SLA is 99.9% monthly for Dedicated with credits as specified in the SOW. We'll attach the SLO table to the redline.
[05:31] Maya: Ok recap — next steps: revised quote, 8k benchmark, network validation, and procurement approver list. Anything else?
[05:38] Ellen: One more thing — can we get a short note on how fallback works if a region saturates? We want deterministic behavior.
[05:46] Jordan: Yes. We can set smart routing to failover to our hosted pool in the same region or to another region. The behavior is configurable: you can prefer latency-first or cost-first. We'll include sample policies in the doc.
[05:59] Ben: Noted.
[06:01] Maya: Great. I'll send the paperwork and the quote today, Jordan will run the benchmark and share perf logs by next week, Rahul and Sofia will handle network and procurement items.
[06:12] Sofia: Will do.
[06:14] Maya: Thanks everyone. End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "kay vee cash"), speaker labels sometimes shifted in automated export.
